Whether you prefer light snacks or filling meals, there’s something for everyone. The lively atmosphere, quick service, and friendly staff make dining here an enjoyable experience.

Food Street isn’t just a place to eat—it’s a celebration of Mumbai’s vibrant street food heritage. Locals come here to relive nostalgic flavors, while visitors get a true introduction to the city’s culinary charm. If you’re in Mumbai and looking for delicious, authentic, and affordable food, Food Street is the perfect stop to satisfy your hunger and enjoy Bombay’s famous taste in every bite.

customer_updates.name: SMRUTISIKHA PRADHAN
customer_updates.text:
• Cannon Pav Bhaji is one of Mumbai's most famous street food destinations, located opposite CSMT.
• Established in 1975 by a former Indian Army veteran, it has been serving Mumbaikars and travelers for decades.
• Known for its rich, buttery, and flavorful pav bhaji made in the traditional Mumbai style.
• The pav is perfectly toasted with butter and pairs wonderfully with the delicious bhaji.
• The place has a unique old-Mumbai charm and is an important part of the city's food heritage.
• Despite being a simple standing food stall, it attracts food lovers from across India.
• Quick service, authentic taste, and a nostalgic atmosphere make the experience memorable.
• A must-visit spot for anyone who wants to enjoy Mumbai's legendary pav bhaji and experience a piece of the city's culinary history.

Overall: Great taste, rich history, and a true Mumbai street-food experience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.review_text: Canon Pav Bhaji did not live up to the hype at all. I have had much better pav bhaji at many other places. I ordered one Amul Butter Pav Bhaji and one Amul Butter Cheese Pav Bhaji. Both were extremely bland and lacked proper spices. There was an excessive amount of butter added, to the point that only butter’s taste was overpowering everything else—no real flavor of the bhaji could be felt. The pav bhaji was not even served properly hot, which made the experience worse. On top of that, the prices are very high for the quality and taste offered. This review is purely based on my personal experience, and unfortunately, it was very disappointing.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Sonawane
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Cannon Pav Bhaji near CST and, unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing. We tried several items Pav Bhaji, Sheera, Sabudana Khichdi and Lassi and to be frank, everything was absolutely tasteless. For a place that is always crowded and located in such a prime spot, I genuinely expected much better in terms of flavour and quality.

The Pav Bhaji lacked the rich, buttery taste and balanced spices that you normally find even at simple street side stalls across Mumbai. The Sheera was bland and lacked the aroma and sweetness that make it enjoyable. Sabudana Khichdi, which is usually comforting and flavourful, felt underwhelming as well. Even the Lassi didn’t have the freshness or thickness you would hope for.

It feels like the only advantage this place has is its central location right outside CST, which naturally attracts tourists and daily commuters. In contrast, some of the other nearby stalls actually serve tastier food at far more economical prices.

Overall, Cannon Pav Bhaji didn’t live up to its hype or its location. If you’re looking for flavourful, satisfying Mumbai street food, you’re better off exploring the smaller stalls around the area.

featured_reviews.name: Vainateya Sahasrabudhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre in Mumbai my grandfather used to take me to have pav bhaji 2000 to 2014. Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a renowned destination for street food enthusiasts, serving mouth-watering pav bhaji that has captured the hearts of many. This iconic eatery has earned a reputation for its delicious food, prompt service, and cozy ambiance.

Ambiance
The ambiance at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is warm and inviting, perfect for a quick bite or a casual meal with friends and family. The decor is minimal, but the vibrant atmosphere and aroma of freshly cooked food make up for it.

Menu and Offerings
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's menu is centered around its signature dish, pav bhaji, which is a flavorful mix of vegetables cooked in a rich tomato-based gravy, served with soft, buttery pav bread. Some popular items on the menu include-
- *Pav Bhaji*: The star of the show, made with a medley of vegetables and spices, served with pav bread.
- *Special Pav Bhaji*: A variation of the classic dish, made with extra butter and spices.

Quality and Taste
The quality and taste of Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre's offerings are exceptional. The pav bhaji is cooked to perfection, with a rich, buttery flavor that's hard to resist. Customers rave about the delicious food, and many have returned for years, making it a testament to the eatery's consistency.

Service
The service at Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is prompt and efficient, ensuring that customers receive their orders quickly and without any hassle. The staff is friendly and courteous, adding to the overall positive experience.

Value for Money
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers excellent value for money, with prices starting from around ₹120-₹200 per person for a meal. Given the quality and quantity of food, it's a steal.

Tips
- Visit Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre during off-peak hours to avoid crowds.
- Try the special pav bhaji for an extra-rich flavor experience.
- Pair your pav bhaji with a buttermilk, lassi or cold drink for a refreshing contrast.

Online Ordering and Delivery
For those who prefer the convenience of home delivery, Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre offers online ordering through platforms like Justdial and Zomato. This allows customers to enjoy their favorite dishes from the comfort of their own homes.

Overall Experience
Cannon Pav Bhaji Centre is a must-visit destination for anyone looking to experience the best of Mumbai's street food scene. With its delicious pav bhaji, prompt service, and excellent value for money, it's a culinary gem that will leave you wanting more.

Rating: 4.5/5 stars.

If you want to eat authentic and affordable pav bhaji in a bustling city like Mumbai, Lenin Pav Bhaji is a must-try place. This place is famous for its bhaji made with Amul Maska and for its reasonable prices. Every customer who comes here feels the taste of the real Mumbai streets with the first bite.

The main identity of Lenin Pav Bhaji is their bhaji dipped in Amul butter. Fresh vegetables — potatoes, peas, tomatoes, bell peppers, and a wonderful blend of spices — are used while preparing the bhaji. The generous use of Amul Maska on it gives the bhaji a creamy, aromatic, and satisfying taste. The crispy pav roasted on a tava, melted butter on top, and a lemon wedge served with it — this experience attracts every customer again and again.

The prices here are another big feature.  The plain pav bhaji costs around ₹70–₹90, while the special Amul pav bhaji costs around ₹110–₹120. These prices are really affordable for such quality taste. This makes this place a good choice for students, workers, and families.

The service is fast, the staff is polite, and the place is always kept clean. Even in a crowded place, the taste and quality are maintained, which is the success of Lenin pav bhaji.

Overall, Lenin pav bhaji is the perfect blend of authentic Mumbai street food, the magic of Amul mask, and affordable pleasure. This place scores 10 out of 10 in all three aspects - taste, quality, and price.

featured_reviews.name: Stringzzz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji – A Legendary Spot for Classic Pav Bhaji Lovers

Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji is a well-known name among street food lovers, especially for those who enjoy rich, buttery, and authentic Mumbai-style Pav Bhaji. Over the years, this place has built a strong reputation for consistent taste, generous portions, and a no-nonsense approach to food. It is a go-to destination for locals and visitors who want to enjoy comforting Indian street food without unnecessary frills.

The highlight here is undoubtedly the Pav Bhaji. The bhaji is thick, flavorful, and perfectly mashed, cooked on a large iron tawa with a generous amount of butter. The blend of vegetables, spices, and butter creates a rich, slightly smoky flavor that reflects the traditional street-style preparation. The spice level is well balanced, making it enjoyable for most palates, while still delivering the bold taste pav bhaji lovers expect.

The pav is soft, fresh, and well toasted with butter, complementing the bhaji beautifully. Each serving comes with chopped onions, lemon, and extra butter on top, allowing customers to customize the taste according to their preference. The consistency of the bhaji is one of the strongest points—neither too watery nor too dry—which shows the experience and skill behind its preparation.

Apart from pav bhaji, Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji is also popular for its dosa varieties. The dosas are crisp, well-cooked, and generously filled, making them a good alternative for those who want something different. However, pav bhaji remains the star dish that draws most of the crowd.

The ambience is simple and functional, typical of a popular street-food-style eatery. Seating is basic, but the focus here is clearly on food quality rather than décor. Despite the constant rush, the place is usually clean, and food preparation can be seen openly, which builds trust among customers.

Service is quick and efficient. Orders are taken promptly, and food is served hot without long waiting times, even during peak hours. The staff is experienced and handles the crowd well, ensuring a smooth flow despite the popularity of the place.

Pricing is reasonable and offers good value for money considering the portion size and taste. Compared to many modern cafés serving pav bhaji at premium prices, Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji delivers authentic flavor at a fair cost, making it accessible to everyone.

Historically, places like Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji represent the true spirit of Indian street food culture—simple ingredients, skilled cooking, and a loyal customer base built over years of trust. Many regular customers associate this place with late-night cravings, family outings, and food memories that bring people back again and again.

Overall, Edward Dosa and Pav Bhaji is a must-visit for anyone who truly appreciates classic pav bhaji. It offers rich taste, consistent quality, quick service, and a nostalgic street-food experience. If you are craving buttery, flavorful pav bhaji that stays true to its roots, this place will not disappoint. 🌶️🧈

featured_reviews.name: Rebecca Lobo
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’d always wanted to visit one of the oldest bakeries in town ,Kyani & Co.and finally got the chance. The ambience is wonderfully nostalgic, filled with old-school charm, and I absolutely loved that part of the experience.

However, the food didn’t quite live up to the hype. The dishes we tried, like the kheema and bhurji, felt quite basic and nothing exceptional. On the brighter side, the snack items were much better , the mawa cake, chicken cutlet, and ,caramel custard were genuinely enjoyable.

Overall, the pricing is reasonable, making it worth a visit for the ambience and certain snacks, but don’t expect too much from the main dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kyani & Co. is a classic Iranian café serving authentic Iranian cuisine. The place is always crowded, and you’ll notice a good mix of locals and foreigners, which shows how popular and well-known it is.

Coming to the food, their chicken dishes stood out. The Chicken Cheese Kebab was actually very nice—it was stuffed with cheese from inside and had a hot-dog–like shape. It felt filling and had a good amount of chicken, which I liked the most.

I also tried the chicken samosa, but I felt the chicken quantity was a bit less, with more masala in the filling. Similarly, the mutton cutlet had more potato than mutton. Personally, I prefer meat-forward dishes.

The ambience is really great with an old-world charm, but photography is not allowed inside. I clicked one photo and was asked not to take pictures, which was a bit disappointing considering how beautiful the place is.

Overall, it’s an authentic Iranian café with a lovely atmosphere. The food is good, especially the chicken items, though the filling ratios may not suit everyone’s taste.

featured_reviews.name: Viraj Redkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Kyani & Co. and honestly, it felt less like a café visit and more like a journey back in time. The moment you walk in, the old-world charm hits you — vintage wooden furniture, classic tiled floors, and an atmosphere that carries stories from over 100 years ago. It’s raw, real, and beautifully untouched.
We ordered the iconic Irani chai, bun maska, and kheema pav — and every bite was pure nostalgia. The chai had that perfect strong, comforting flavor, the bun maska was soft with just the right amount of buttery goodness, and the kheema pav was rich, flavorful, and absolutely satisfying.
What makes this place special isn’t just the food — it’s the experience. No fancy frills, no modern distractions, just timeless simplicity done right.
A small heads-up: it’s strictly cash only — no cards, no UPI — which somehow adds to its old-school vibe.
If you’re in Mumbai and want to experience something authentic, soulful, and truly fascinating, this place is not just a café… it’s a legacy you can taste.

From vada pav and frankies to rolls, Chinese, and late-night snacks, every stall has its own loyal crowd and its own story. Standing on the road, eating with one hand and holding the plate with the other, conversations flow naturally and memories get made. We waited for more than 45 minutes after placing our order, yet no food was served. Despite multiple follow-ups with the staff and management, there was little concern shown and no proper update on the delay. Customers should not have to repeatedly chase the staff just to get basic service.

To make matters worse, some of the plates and serving ware appeared chipped and damaged, which raises serious concerns about hygiene and attention to detail.

While the food itself was good when it finally arrived, the poor service, lack of communication, and overall management of the dining experience completely overshadowed it. A restaurant's responsibility goes beyond good food it also includes timely service, cleanliness, and customer care, all of which were lacking during this visit.

Unfortunately, not an experience I would recommend until significant improvements are made.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been coming here since I was a kid—long enough that I’m pretty sure my first real chicken tandoori happened right here. The menu has changed over the years, sure, but the place has stubbornly refused to lose its old-school charm. Portions? Still generous. This isn’t food that apologizes for itself.

The Chinese starters have absolutely nothing to do with China—and thank God for that. They’re loud, greasy, Indo-Chinese comfort bombs that slap hard. Pick any of the chicken gravies and you’re in a good place emotionally. I will say this: the kebabs feel a little smaller than they used to. Shrinkflation? Age? Betrayal? I don’t know. Still good. Just… noted.

Twenty-one years ago, when I was a broke college student and my parents would leave town—trusting me alone at home far more than they should have—I ordered from here like it was a civic duty. My friends from that era still remember how much food I could put away from this place. This is not health food. No one here is pretending otherwise. But it hits all the right buttons.

I ordered so often that before food apps, before algorithms, the guy answering the phone knew my order just by hearing my voice. Within an hour, like clockwork, the food would land at my parents’ place. I’d sit there demolishing it while binge-watching American TV, living my best irresponsible life.

Some of my old favorites are gone now, but the current menu holds its own. I’ve eaten here with my wife, with her family, across decades and phases of life. Parking is usually manageable. There’s a mosque nearby, Bombay Hospital around the corner, and the now-shuttered Liberty Cinema—where I watched half my childhood movies. The area isn’t glamorous. It doesn’t try to be. It’s old Mumbai, still breathing, still feeding people properly.

This place survives because it’s trusted. Because it’s consistent. Because people who know food still show up here quietly and eat without drama.

What’s instantly noticeable is who eats here.
Old-school locals, serious food people, and a steady stream of expats—especially Arab expats—who clearly didn’t wander in by accident.

Late at night, you’ll see many happy Muslim families settling in comfortably, sharing plates, unhurried, treating the place like an extension of home.

Go without hesitation.
Ask the manager what to order.

Then sit down and let them take care of you.

Had a good overall experience at Pancharatna Restaurant & Bar. The ambience inside is really nice and gives a pleasant vibe. It’s a good place to sit and relax with friends or family. Coming to the food – the taste was good overall. The chicken dishes were nice and spicy, just the way we liked them. However, the garlic naan was not that great; it was quite chewy and could have been better. The rest of the food was satisfying.

The pricing is moderate – not too expensive, not too cheap – reasonable for the quality and ambience.

Overall, it was a good experience, and I would consider visiting again.

I visited this place with my best friend on a Thursday evening this week.

It turned out to be their Thursday candle light dinner special with guitar and live singing, which we were not aware of.

Just 2 friends enjoying their beer in a dim ambience and an amazing Artist performing that evening (sorry, I don't know the name of the Artist). He was just awesome both locally and with guitar. He just set the whole vibe of that evening. Kudos to that!

If you order alcohol. You get unlimited Chakna (sides slong-with the alcohol), i.e., Salted peanuts, green salad, corn salad and papad with green chutney, all of this unlimited. They refill as soon as they see the bowls are empty.

Order took time to arrive, but continuous chakna refills made it easier to wait.

Staff is courteous and polite.

We ordered:
* Panchratna fried chicken 3/5 (they should serve this with a honey mustard dip or a tandoori Mayo dip, but they don't serve this with a dip by default). If you ask for a ketchup or a Schezwan sauce, you ll get it with no extra charges (points for that).

* Panchratna classic chicken Biryani, served  since decades 3/5

Location of the bar is a bit tricky as it is slightly inside the lane. Just get into the lane adjacent to Jaffer Bhai restaurant in Marine Lines, close to Bombay Hospital and you will see the bar right infront of you on the left hand side.

Overall. It was a very nice experience, must visit with friends or family.

Please note, my experience was totally based on a Thursday evening live singing vibe. Other days might have a different vibe.
